title: Who Can Claim Maintenance From a Father-in-Law's Estate?
desc: The Supreme Court held on 13 January 2026 that a widowed daughter-in-law can claim maintenance from her father-in-law's estate under section 21 of HAMA, 1956.
why: A Supreme Court ruling of 13 January 2026 settled a question that comes up often in Uttarakhand families: can a daughter-in-law still claim support from her father-in-law's property after her husband dies?
keyPoints: The Supreme Court held that a widowed daughter-in-law is a dependant under section 21 of the Hindu Adoptions and Maintenance Act, 1956.
It does not matter whether she became a widow before or after her father-in-law's death; the claim still stands.
The claim is against the heirs who inherit the estate, and can only be raised after the father-in-law has died.
She must show she cannot maintain herself from her husband's estate, her own earnings, or her children.

sections.h: Can a widow claim maintenance from her father-in-law's estate?
p: Yes. The Supreme Court held on 13 January 2026, in a ruling under the Hindu Adoptions and Maintenance Act, 1956, that a daughter-in-law who becomes a widow only after her father-in-law's death can still claim maintenance (financial support) from his estate under section 21(vii). The timing of her husband's death does not change this. In Uttarakhand, such a claim is usually filed before the Family Court at Haldwani or the civil court that handles maintenance matters.

The case involved a father-in-law who died in December 2021. One son had already died before him; a second son died a little over a year later. The second son's widow sought maintenance from the father-in-law's estate, and the matter went up to the Supreme Court on the question of whether she qualified as a dependant at all.

sections.h: Who counts as a dependant, and who has to pay?
p: Section 21 of the Act lists dependants of a Hindu who has died, including a widowed daughter-in-law, parents, and minor children. To qualify, she must show she cannot support herself from her own earnings or property, her late husband's estate, or her children.

Section 22 puts the duty to maintain these dependants on the heirs who inherit the deceased's estate, out of the property they received. The Supreme Court clarified that this claim can only be raised after the father-in-law's death, not before.
The Court also said that reading the law to exclude a daughter-in-law widowed after her father-in-law's death would be unfair and against the right to equality and dignity under the Constitution.

whatToDo: Keep a record of the family's property and who holds it now, including revenue records and any will.
Gather proof of your own income, or lack of it, and of your late husband's assets, since the claim depends on showing you cannot otherwise maintain yourself.
File the maintenance claim before the Family Court or civil court with jurisdiction over the estate; there is no fixed limitation period under this Act, but delay can weaken a claim.
Take legal advice on your own facts, since the amount and the specific heirs liable depend on the size and division of the estate.

hi.title: ससुर की संपत्ति से भरण-पोषण कौन मांग सकता है?
keyPoints: सुप्रीम कोर्ट ने कहा है कि विधवा बहू हिंदू दत्तक ग्रहण और भरण-पोषण अधिनियम, 1956 की धारा 21 के तहत आश्रित मानी जाएगी।
वह ससुर की मृत्यु से पहले विधवा हुई हो या बाद में, इससे फर्क नहीं पड़ता।
यह दावा संपत्ति पाने वाले उत्तराधिकारियों के खिलाफ, ससुर की मृत्यु के बाद ही किया जा सकता है।
उसे यह दिखाना होगा कि वह अपने पति की संपत्ति, अपनी कमाई या बच्चों से अपना गुजारा नहीं कर पा रही।
p: 13 जनवरी 2026 के इस फैसले में सुप्रीम कोर्ट ने स्पष्ट किया कि विधवा बहू को उसके ससुर की संपत्ति से भरण-पोषण पाने का अधिकार है, चाहे वह पति की मृत्यु ससुर से पहले हो या बाद में।
